clue.text: Laugh showing endless pleasure at end of concert

indicators.note: the trimmed word for pleasure is placed after the word for concert

parts.note: a gig is a pop or rock concert

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the word for pleasure is dropped

parts.note: glee is delight or pleasure

explanation.surface: Someone at a concert laughs, showing their delight right through to the final number.
explanation.definitionFit: A giggle is a light, silly kind of laugh, so the noun fits directly.

clue.text: Estimated almost five hundred, presumably, can be accommodated in B and B?

indicators.note: the money word is put up inside the shortened word for estimated
almost the whole word, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: guessed means estimated
a thou is a thousand; the setter's 'presumably' hints the figure is loose, the blog reading it as half a thou

explanation.surface: Someone guesses nearly five hundred guests could stay at a bed and breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims GUESSED to GUESSE. The money piece is loose: THOU means a thousand, and 'presumably' admits the figure is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed and breakfast is a small lodging business, which is an example of a guesthouse.

clue.text: Crawl, losing footing in wood

indicators.note: losing its foot, the bottom letter in a down entry, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to grovel is to crawl or fawn

explanation.surface: Someone crawls and slips over among the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A grove is a small group of trees, so a small wood.

clue.text: Money you say father needed for kiddie's treat?

indicators.note: you say signals a word spoken, the sound kept but the spelling changed

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money
pop is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad needs cash, you claim, for a child's sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a sweet on a stick, a classic children's treat.

clue.text: Nosh includes meat cooked very hot?

indicators.note: the word for nosh contains the meat within it

parts.note: a feed is a meal, informal nosh
lamb is a meat

explanation.surface: A meal featuring meat that has been cooked at fierce heat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as playful: flambéed food is set alight with spirit, which is cooking very hot indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Food flambéed is doused in brandy and set alight, a cheeky description of cooking at high heat.

clue.text: Fifty sheep in English market town

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty
ewes are female sheep

explanation.surface: Fifty sheep are on sale in an English market town.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewes is the county town of East Sussex in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewes is a historic town in Sussex with a long-standing market, so a market town.

clue.text: Importance of sign in middle of mountain

indicators.note: the sign sits in the middle of the abbreviation

parts.note: MT is the abbreviation for mount or mountain
an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: The significance of a signal halfway up a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Moment means importance or weight, as in a matter of great moment.

clue.text: Great delight, accepting very good beauty treatment?

indicators.note: the word for delight takes in the very good letters

parts.note: elation is great joy
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by a salon procedure that went very well.
explanation.definitionFit: Epilation is removing body hair, a cosmetic procedure offered in beauty salons.

clue.text: Notes in overtures to Donizetti operas harmoniously sung

indicators.note: overtures open an opera, so the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Musical notes in the opening pieces of Donizetti's operas, sung in harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Doh is the first note of the sol-fa scale, so dohs are musical notes.

clue.text: Parisian landmark where Europeans accept work

indicators.note: the pair of Europeans take the word for work between them

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, so two Europeans give two Es
toil is hard work

explanation.surface: A spot in Paris where Europeans put up with labour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Étoile is the great circle in Paris around the Arc de Triomphe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Étoile, now Place Charles de Gaulle, is a famous Paris square, so it counts as a landmark.

clue.text: Pop off to join school activities?

definitions.meaning: to pop off is to die, slang for being killed in gangster talk
a school is a group of fish, so joining one means swimming among them

explanation.surface: A child dashes away to take part in after-school clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a place of lessons but is a shoal of fish. The gangster idiom, more often 'sleep with the fishes', means to be dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangland idiom for being killed and dumped in water, so a euphemism for dying.

clue.text: Idea's incomplete, however

indicators.note: not complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a thought is an idea

explanation.surface: The idea is unfinished, nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: Though used at the end of a sentence means nevertheless, a synonym of however.

clue.text: See 10
Welsh town needing hospital orderly

indicators.note: needing here means lacking, so the hospital letter is taken away

parts.note: Neath is a town in south Wales

explanation.surface: A Welsh town in need of a hospital orderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orderly' looks like a hospital worker, a noun, but it is the adjective meaning tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and orderly are synonyms, both meaning tidy and well arranged.

clue.text: In Scottish island get rid of right modern building?

indicators.note: the discarding word goes in the island's name

parts.note: Skye is an island of the Scottish Hebrides
to scrap something is to discard it

explanation.surface: On a Scottish island, someone tears down something correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A skyscraper is a very tall building, typical of modern cities, hence the hedging question mark.

clue.text: Not at home, eating crackers?

definitions.meaning: literally, away having a midday meal out
crackers is slang for mad, and the phrase also means dotty or eccentric

explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like biscuits to eat, but it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, gone out for the midday meal; as slang, dotty or not all there, matching crackers.

clue.text: Shattered president's heading off, showing fatigue

indicators.note: something shattered is broken to pieces, so the letters are rearranged
the head, the first letter, of the word president's is taken away

explanation.surface: An exhausted head of state takes off, looking weary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shattered' looks like a synonym for exhausted but is the anagram signal, working on RESIDENTS once 'heading off' removes P.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness and fatigue are synonyms for weariness.

clue.text: South of river traveller reversed vehicle

indicators.note: in a down entry, the turned word sits below the river

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

indicators.note: the word for traveller is read backwards

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is a commercial traveller

explanation.surface: South of the river, a traveller backs up a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' looks like a driving manoeuvre but turns REP round.
explanation.definitionFit: A camper is a camper van, a vehicle fitted for living in.

clue.text: Choose film with shock ending

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film

indicators.note: ending signals the final letter of the word shock

explanation.surface: Select a movie that has a startling finale.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick and to choose are synonyms, both meaning to select.

clue.text: Highly-poisonous compound, portion with water put in

indicators.note: the water is placed inside the portion

parts.note: a part is a portion
aqua is Latin for water

explanation.surface: A dose of a deadly chemical diluted with some water.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraquat is a weedkiller notorious for being highly toxic to people, a poisonous chemical compound.

clue.text: European composer Bach eclipses

indicators.note: eclipses means covers up, so the words composer Bach conceal the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A European composer outshines Bach.
explanation.definitionFit: A Serb is a person from Serbia, a European nation.

clue.text: Celebratory drinks winner's taken with woman

parts.note: a champ, short for champion, is a winner
Agnes is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A victor has taken drinks to celebrate with a female companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagnes are sparkling wines traditionally drunk to celebrate, so they are celebratory drinks.

clue.text: Unproductive noble, according to reports

indicators.note: as reported, the word is heard rather than read, so it sounds the same

parts.note: a baron is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A nobleman, so people say, achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren land yields nothing, so it is unproductive.

clue.text: Poetry collection doing the rounds in summer mostly

indicators.note: turning round, so the shortened word is read backwards
most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a summer is one who sums, an adder

explanation.surface: An anthology of verse passed around for most of the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' looks like the season but is one who adds up. 'mostly' trims ADDER to ADDE, which 'doing the rounds' turns back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is the Old Norse collection of mythological and heroic poems.

clue.text: Here get extra land developed to accommodate a military commander

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the single letter a
developed means worked into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Here the conqueror acquires additional territory, built up to house an army chief.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of HEREGETEXTRALAND, signalled by 'developed', takes A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Macedonian king who conquered much of the known world is history's best known military commander.

clue.text: Publicity about American president

indicators.note: the publicity goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: ads, advertisements, are publicity

explanation.surface: Advertising surrounding a US head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and John Quincy Adams were both US presidents, so a president by example.

clue.text: Lady excited northern singer

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman is thrilled by a vocalist from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Dylan is a famous singer-songwriter, so the name is an example of a singer.

clue.text: Try various tablets in reduced quantity

indicators.note: only a small portion of the words various tablets is taken, the letters lying within them

explanation.surface: Sample different pills, but take a smaller dose.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to try it, so the noun means an attempt.

clue.text: See 24
Bit of exercise, going forwards and backwards

indicators.note: the word reads the same in either direction, which this phrase signals

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An exercise that involves moving to and fro.
explanation.definitionFit: A pull-up is a gym exercise, hauling the body up to a bar, so it is one bit of exercise.

clue.text: One head backing transport company

indicators.note: the other pieces come behind the transport, supporting it from the rear

parts.note: a bus is a means of transport
I is the Roman numeral one
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour names like Sheerness

explanation.surface: One manager supports a transport firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a boss but is a headland, NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A business is a firm or commercial enterprise, the same as a company.

clue.text: No rest, sadly, for drug addict

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An addict gets no respite, unfortunately.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoner is slang for someone who habitually uses cannabis, a loose fit for an addict.
